data-peek 

 
 A fast, keyboard-first SQL client for PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, SQLite, and ClickHouse (beta). 
 Open it, run the query, get the answer, get back to work.
 

 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 Website ·
 Download ·
 Docs ·
 Changelog 
 

 
 Black Friday: Pro is 40% off from 26 Nov to 1 Dec, applied at checkout.
 

 
 
 
 
 

 Why data-peek

- Fast. Opens in about two seconds and stays light on memory. No splash screens, no project setup.
- Keyboard-first. Cmd/Ctrl+K switches connections and opens tabs, saved queries, and settings. Every shortcut is documented.
- Local and private. Credentials are encrypted with your OS keychain. No telemetry, no account, no cloud sync.
- Grows with the task. A quick SELECT stays quick, and query plans, live diffs, ER diagrams, and an AI assistant are there when the job gets bigger.

 Install

 Platform Command 
 -------------------- -------------------------------------------------------------- 
 macOS, Linux curl -fsSL \ sh 
 Windows (PowerShell) irm \ iex 
 macOS (Homebrew) brew install --cask Rohithgilla12/tap/data-peek 

Or grab a build from Releases: .dmg for macOS (signed and notarised), .exe for Windows, and .AppImage , .deb , or .tar.gz for Linux.

 
 Platform notes 

 macOS. Builds are signed and notarised, so they open without warnings. The quick installer installs the matching .dmg and clears the quarantine flag for you. If an older manual install says the app is "damaged", run xattr -cr "/Applications/Data Peek.app" .

 Linux. The AppImage and the .deb update themselves; .tar.gz installs need a manual download for each new release. The quick installer puts the AppImage at /.local/bin/data-peek . The .deb installs to /opt/data-peek with an AppArmor profile, which Ubuntu 24.04+ needs for Electron's sandbox.

 

 No install: npx @data-peek/cli doctor 

Eight Postgres schema checks from the terminal. Each finding comes with the SQL that fixes it.

 

It finds tables without a primary key, foreign keys without an index, duplicate, unused, and invalid indexes, bloat, never-vacuumed tables, and nullable foreign keys. These are the same checks as Schema Intel in the app. See packages/cli .

 
 
 

 See it work

 
 
 
 
 Watch Mode : pin a SELECT and watch cells change live.
 
 
 
 Query plans : EXPLAIN ANALYZE as a tree, with the slow node and its fix.
 
 
 
 
 
 MCP server : agents can read freely; every write waits for your approval.
 
 
 
 Time Machine : scrub back through past results and diff any two runs.
 
 
 

More clips (command palette, ER diagrams, the AI assistant, inline editing) are on datapeek.dev.

 Features

 Query editor

- Monaco editor with schema-aware autocomplete that understands table aliases
- Multiple tabs and windows, plus cross-tab references: name a tab and query its result from another as @name 
- Step through multi-statement scripts one statement at a time, with manual transactions on PostgreSQL
- Saved queries with folders and tags, reusable snippets, and SQL notebooks that mix SQL cells with Markdown
- A sidebar omnibar ( / ) that searches tables, columns, functions, saved queries, and history

 Results and data

- Inline editing with a preview of the generated INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE before you commit
- Smart filters and sorting on results without re-running the query
- Spreadsheet-style cell selection with live sum and average, find across every page of a result ( Cmd/Ctrl+F in the grid), and copy a selection as TSV, CSV, JSON, or Markdown
- Foreign key navigation, a JSON/JSONB editor, and one-click column statistics
- Export to CSV, JSON, SQL INSERT s, or Markdown, or share a result as an image
- CSV import with column mapping and type inference, PostgreSQL .sql dump import, and an FK-aware fake data generator
- Data masking that blurs sensitive columns for demos and screenshots

 Performance

- EXPLAIN ANALYZE viewer with an interactive plan tree on PostgreSQL
- Query telemetry with a timing waterfall, and a benchmark mode reporting avg/p90/p95/p99
- Performance hints for missing indexes, N+1 patterns, and slow queries, each with a suggested fix
- On ClickHouse, performance analysis flags reads that skip few granules and summarizes past runs from system.query log 
- Cancel a running query, or kill a blocking one from the health monitor

 Live data

- Watch Mode re-runs a read-only query every 500 ms to 5 min and highlights changed cells. It refuses to poll anything that writes.
- Time Machine snapshots past results locally, so you can scrub back and diff any two runs ( Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+H )
- Scheduled queries on a cron, with run history and desktop notifications
- PostgreSQL LISTEN / NOTIFY with a live event log
- Dashboards built from your queries, with charts, KPIs, and tables

 Schema and monitoring

- Schema explorer for tables, views, functions, procedures, triggers, and sequences
- Table designer for creating and altering tables: columns, indexes, and constraints
- Interactive ER diagrams
- Health monitor with active queries, table sizes, cache hit ratios, and lock detection
- Schema Intel diagnostics for unindexed foreign keys, duplicate or unused indexes, missing primary keys, and table bloat, with suggested SQL fixes

 AI and agents

 

- Ask is the default tab ( Cmd/Ctrl+T ). One input takes a question or SQL. SQL runs directly. A question goes to your AI, which writes the SQL, runs it when it only reads, and explains what came back with a table, chart, or number. Writes wait for you to click Run, and a failed query has a one-click fix. The plain SQL editor is Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+T .
- Ask from anywhere: type a question into Cmd/Ctrl+K , pick Ask about this table in the schema tree, or click Fix with AI on a failed query
- In the SQL editor, Cmd/Ctrl+I rewrites the query or the selection from a sentence and shows the change as a diff to accept or reject
- AI assistant that turns plain English into SQL and builds charts from results. It knows your schema.
- Runs on the Claude Code, Codex, or Antigravity subscr

Platform notes

Eight Postgres schema checks from the terminal. Each finding comes with the SQL that fixes it.

npx @data-peek/cli doctor postgres://user:pass@localhost:5432/app

A question goes to your AI, which writes the SQL, runs it when it only reads, and explains what came back with a table, chart, or number.   • A built-in MCP server (off by default) that exposes your connections to AI agents. Reads are capped and run read-only, and every write needs your approval in the app.

  • PostgreSQL, MySQL, Microsoft SQL Server, SQLite, and ClickHouse. ClickHouse support is in beta and covers querying and browsing, so inline editing and the table designer stay off for ClickHouse connections.
  • SSH tunnels through bastion hosts, using a password or a key
  • Credentials encrypted with the OS keychain, and no telemetry
  • An optional tamper-evident audit log of every statement you run. It stays local.

The docs cover every feature in depth.
